# Results — Study 150 (SAD-Effect) on the Shiller S&P 500 monthly tape

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). Three tests of the
Kamstra-Kramer-Levi (2003) Seasonal Affective Disorder hypothesis — seasonal split of
monthly returns, OLS regression on a daylight-change proxy, and a SAD calendar strategy
vs buy-and-hold — all run on the Shiller S&P 500 monthly total-return series.
As-of **2026-06-14**.*

## Data stamp

| Source | Window | n months | Fingerprint |
|---|---|---|---|
| Shiller S&P 500 monthly (shared cache `_cache/shiller_sp500.parquet`) | 1871-02 to 2026-05 | 1,864 | `7f61641a8936` |

Total return = monthly price appreciation + lagged monthly dividend yield (Dividend / Price / 12).
Rows with SP500 = 0 (recent placeholder rows) are dropped.

## Test 1 — Seasonal split vs the unconditional monthly mean

KKL prediction: SAD-onset months (Sep-Nov, days shortening) should have *below*-average returns;
recovery months (Dec-Mar, returning daylight) should have *above*-average returns.

| Group | n | Mean (bps/month) | Welch t vs unconditional |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| **SAD onset (Sep-Nov)** | 465 | **+53.8** | **-1.31** |
| **SAD recovery (Dec-Mar)** | 622 | **+94.1** | **+0.68** |
| Summer (Apr-Aug) | 777 | +91.5 | +0.47 |
| **Unconditional** | 1,864 | **+83.0** | — |

- Onset is below-average (+53.8 vs +83.0 bps) but the gap is **not significant** (|t| = 1.31 < 2).
- Recovery is barely above-average, also **not significant** (t = 0.68).
- Summer is above average too — suggesting the onset gap is not a distinctive SAD signal
  but rather autumn weakness shared with other known seasonals (harvest, end-of-fiscal-year).

## Test 2 — Daylight-change regression (KKL's core specification)

OLS regression of monthly total return on the month-over-month change in astronomical
day-length hours (40°N, the 15th of each month). KKL predicts a **positive** slope.

| Metric | Value |
|---|--:|
| Slope (bps per hour of daylight change) | +0.183 |
| HAC (Newey-West) t-stat on slope | **+0.16** |
| R² | 0.000 |
| n | 1,863 |

The daylight proxy explains essentially **zero** variance in monthly returns and its slope
is completely indistinguishable from zero (t = 0.16). The KKL regression mechanism has
no empirical support over the full 155-year sample.

## Sub-period breakdown (the data-mining story)

| Period | n | Onset t | Recovery t | Daylight slope t |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 1871-1949 (pre-KKL) | 947 | -0.82 | +0.03 | -0.53 |
| **1950-2002 (KKL sample)** | **636** | **-1.12** | **+1.83** | **+1.27** |
| 2003-2026 (post-publication) | 281 | -0.26 | -0.85 | +0.11 |
| Full 1871-2026 | 1,864 | -1.31 | +0.68 | +0.16 |

The KKL sample (1950-2002) shows the strongest recovery signal (t = 1.83) and daylight
regression (t = 1.27) — both still **below the |t| >= 2 bar** even in their own sample.
Before their sample the effect is absent; after it (2003-2026) it reverses for the recovery
group (t = -0.85). This is the classic signature of **data mining / in-sample over-fit**:
a weak pattern in one sample period, absent before, and reversed after.

## Test 3 — SAD calendar strategy vs buy-and-hold

Hold equities only in SAD-recovery months (Dec-Mar), cash (0%) otherwise. The honest
baseline is buy-and-hold, which captures all 12 months of the equity risk premium.

| Strategy | CAGR | Ann. Sharpe | HAC t | Max drawdown |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **SAD calendar (Dec-Mar only)** | **3.6%** | **0.55** | +6.01 | -31.1% |
| **Buy-and-hold** | **9.4%** | **0.71** | +7.33 | -81.7% |

The SAD strategy's CAGR (3.6%) is **less than half of buy-and-hold (9.4%)** because it sits
in cash for 8 of 12 months, missing the bulk of the equity risk premium. Its Sharpe (0.55)
is also below buy-and-hold (0.71). Even if the seasonal pattern were real, holding only
4 winter months is dominated by simply owning the market.

## Synthetic positive control

The machinery is confirmed functional: on a synthetic tape with ``sad_premium_bp = 40``,
the planted signal is detectable (recovery t > 0 directionally, daylight slope t > 1).
On the null (premium = 0), t-stats are noise. The real tape matches the null.

## Verdict

- **Signal — NONE.** The SAD seasonal in monthly returns is not statistically significant
  over the full 155-year Shiller tape: onset t = -1.31, recovery t = +0.68, daylight
  regression t = +0.16. All fall short of |t| >= 2. Sub-period analysis shows the
  strongest signal appeared in KKL's own 1950-2002 sample (and only marginally), with
  the effect absent before and reversed after publication — a data-mining fingerprint.
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.** Even if the seasonal were real, the SAD calendar strategy
  (hold Dec-Mar only) achieves CAGR 3.6% vs buy-and-hold's 9.4%, and Sharpe 0.55 vs
  0.71. Sitting out 8 months of positive equity returns is not a winning strategy.
- **Data-mining critique (Kelly-Meschke 2010): CONFIRMED.** The effect barely appeared
  in-sample, is absent out-of-sample, and is entangled with the January effect and
  Halloween seasonality — not cleanly attributable to SAD.
